summary: The broken calculator just skips every `0` digit, so we treat the number as text and delete the zeros (T2 — digit manipulation). String tools make digit problems one-liners.

blocks.title: Keep the number as a string
blocks.text: No `int()` here — we only need the digits, and `str.replace` works on text. `.strip()` removes stray spaces so they don't show up in the output.

blocks.title: Remove every zero and print
blocks.text: `n.replace('0', '')` returns a copy with all `'0'` characters removed: `'40507'` → `'457'`. Doing this with `% 10` and `// 10` math works too, but it is longer and easy to rebuild backwards.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 10 digits — instant.
pitfalls: Rebuilding the number with `% 10` math and getting the digits reversed.
